forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

domain_restrictions: X must be finite so that the sum over X is well defined.
w takes only the two integer values plus 1 and minus 1.
iota maps each element of X back into X.
The relation iota of iota of x equals x holds for every x in X, so iota is an involution.
The sign reversal condition is required only for nonfixed points, meaning points x with iota of x not equal to x.
The value plus 1 is required at fixed points, meaning points x with iota of x equal to x.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For a finite set X, an involution iota on X, and a function w from X to plus or minus 1 that changes sign along nonfixed iota pairs and equals plus 1 at fixed points, the total sum of w over X is exactly the number of fixed points of iota. Therefore that sum is a nonnegative integer.
quantifier_order: Let X be a finite set.
Let w be a function from X to plus or minus 1.
Let iota be a function from X to X.
For every x in X, iota of iota of x equals x.
For every x in X, if iota of x is not equal to x, then w of iota of x equals minus w of x.
For every x in X, if iota of x equals x, then w of x equals plus 1.
Then the sum of w over X equals the number of fixed points of iota.

payload.statement_nl: Let X be a finite set and let w : X -> { -1, +1 } be a sign function. Suppose iota : X -> X satisfies iota(iota(x)) = x for every x in X, w(iota(x)) = -w(x) whenever iota(x) != x, and w(x) = +1 whenever iota(x) = x. Then sum_{x in X} w(x) = |{x in X : iota(x) = x}|. In particular, sum_{x in X} w(x) is a nonnegative integer.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let F := {x in X : iota(x) = x} be the set of fixed points, and let M := X \ F. Since X is finite, both F and M are finite, and X is the disjoint union F ⊔ M. Therefore
sum_{x in X} w(x) = sum_{x in F} w(x) + sum_{x in M} w(x).

First consider F. By hypothesis, whenever iota(x) = x we have w(x) = +1. Hence every term in the sum over F equals 1, so
sum_{x in F} w(x) = |F|.

Now consider M. If x belongs to M, then iota(x) != x. Also iota(iota(x)) = x, so iota(x) is again in M; thus each x in M belongs to a two-element set {x, iota(x)}. Let
O := { {x, iota(x)} : x in M }.
Each member of O has exactly two elements, because x != iota(x) for x in M. Moreover, O is a partition of M: every x in M lies in {x, iota(x)}, and if two such sets intersect, then they are equal. Indeed, if z lies in both {x, iota(x)} and {y, iota(y)}, then {x, iota(x)} = {z, iota(z)} and also {y, iota(y)} = {z, iota(z)}, so the two sets are equal.

Since O partitions M, we may sum over its blocks:
sum_{x in M} w(x) = sum_{A in O} sum_{x in A} w(x).
For any block A in O, write A = {x, iota(x)} with x in M. Then iota(x) != x, so the sign-reversal hypothesis applies and gives w(iota(x)) = -w(x). Therefore
sum_{y in A} w(y) = w(x) + w(iota(x)) = w(x) - w(x) = 0.
Thus every block contributes 0, and consequently
sum_{x in M} w(x) = 0.

Combining the two parts,
sum_{x in X} w(x) = |F| + 0 = |F| = |{x in X : iota(x) = x}|.
This proves the stated identity. In particular, the sum is the cardinality of a finite set, hence a nonnegative integer.
result_payload.proof_summary: Partition X into fixed points and 2-cycles of the involution. Fixed points contribute +1 each, while each nonfixed pair {x, iota(x)} contributes w(x)+w(iota(x)) = 0. Therefore the total sum equals the number of fixed points.
